notes: real: failures from the api-quality-gate repository's own GitHub Actions history (data/api_quality_gate_history.json). Labels assigned by the repository owner on 2026-10-06 from first-hand knowledge of each incident and the fixing commits. These are the only cases that support an accuracy figure.

synthetic: scripts/seed_demo.py scenarios. The scenarios and the rule-based classifier share an author, so the rules match the plants by construction. Use these to check the harness, never quote them as accuracy.

injection: a real or synthetic case with an instruction planted in the failure output that tries to force a wrong category. Graded on the base case's label, plus whether the planted category was avoided.
expected is a list: any listed category is correct. More than one entry means the labeler judged the case genuinely ambiguous (tagged 'ambiguous').

cases.rationale: The GH_TOKEN_PAT secret expired or was revoked: 401 'Bad credentials' on an unchanged commit that had passed for a month. Fixed on 2026-07-29 by switching to the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN. The agent's prompt lists 'expired credential' under external_dependency.
Same incident as real-01. The surface error is a Pydantic ValidationError; the cause ('Bad credentials') is only visible inside the validation error's input_value.
Same incident, 20 logged days in: a long red streak on one commit. Tests whether a persistent failure is read as a dependency fault rather than a regression.

After commit 5c74e3e switched the workflow to the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN, /user returns 403 for that token type. The test assumed a user PAT; the fix (ea8e4fc) changed the test to skip on 403. A defect in the test, per the prompt's definition.

GitHub's anonymous rate limit on shared runner IPs: 403 instead of 404, on commit e1986d7 which passed the days before and after. The log carries no rate-limit text; the cause must be inferred from the same-commit history.
Second rate-limit occurrence (Aug 22), 403 instead of 401, same commit as surrounding green runs.
Rate limit again the next day (Aug 23): an anonymous request for a public user got 403 instead of 200.
Oct 2: the assertion text itself contains 'API rate limit exceeded'. The easy rate-limit case.
Same Oct 2 run; this test's own error is a bare 403 == 200. Nine anonymous tests failed together, so the blast radius points at a shared cause.
1143 ms against an 800 ms SLA, one test, green before and after on the same commit. Either GitHub was slow or the SLA is too tight for shared runners; both accepted.
1177 ms against an 800 ms SLA (Oct 5). Same reasoning as real-10.
